#  Otter.ai Public API 

Otter Help

 October 29, 2026 20:46 Updated 

Otter.ai’s Public API provides programmatic access to retrieve channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details from your Otter account.

 Getting Started: Otter's Public API is available for all Enterprise workspaces. If you do not see this feature for your workspace, contact your Otter account manager.

## API Fundamentals

Essential information for authenticating, paging through results, and understanding usage limits.

##  Authentication Create and manage your API keys 

All API requests require authentication using Bearer token authentication. Follow the steps below to create your API key. 

1. Go to Integrations → Developer.  
2. Click Create key.
3. Click Copy and store the API key in a safe place.

 Note: This is only visible once. Make sure you copy the API key in this pop-up. If you forget to copy, follow steps 1-3 to create another key.
4. The API key can now be used. Follow steps 1-4 to create another API key.

 Note: There is a limit of 2 API keys per user.

Using your API key:

Include your API key in the Authorization header for every request:

```plaintext
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

✅ Security best practices:

- Never share your API key publicly or commit it to version control
- Store API keys securely using environment variables or secrets management
- Rotate API keys periodically

## Rate Limits

Enterprise plan users are currently limited to 10 requests / second. If you exceed your rate limit, you'll receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response.

...

### `GET /channels`

Use this endpoint to list channels for the authenticated user. Results are returned in alphabetical order by channel name.

Example Request:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.otter.ai/v1/channels" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

...

##  Conversations Endpoints to create, list, and retrieve conversations, including conversation details and audio downloads 

- `POST /conversations`
- `GET /conversations`
- `GET /conversations/{id}`
- `GET /conversations/{id}/audio`

### `POST /conversations`

Creates a new conversation from a file. This is useful if you are importing calls into Otter, such as from a Dialer.

Request Body:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | string (URL) | Yes | URL to the file to process |
| `name` | string | No | Name for the conversation |

Example Request:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.otter.ai/v1/conversations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "file": "https://example.com/file.mp4",
    "name": "Product Launch Meeting"
  }'
```

Response: Returns a `ConversationCreateResponse` with status.

...

{
 "status": "success",
 "completed_at": "2025-12-01 01:00:00Z",
 "file": "audio.mp3"
}
```

### `GET /conversations`

Use this endpoint to list conversations for the authenticated user. Results are returned in reverse chronological order (most recent first) and use cursor-based pagination for efficient retrieval. You can optionally include shared conversations or filter results by channel.

 Tip: Use workspace webhooks to receive Conversation data in real-time!

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| include_shared | boolean | No | Whether to include conversations shared with the user. Default: false. Automatically set to true if channel_id is provided |
| channel_id | string | No | Filter conversations by channel ID. Overrides include_shared |
| limit | integer | No | Number of items to return per page. Minimum: 1, Maximum: 20 |
| cursor | string | No | Cursor for pagination. Use the next_cursor value from the previous response to retrieve the next page |

Example Request:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.otter.ai/v1/conversations?include_shared=false&channel_id=&limit=20&cursor=" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

...

### `GET /conversations/{id}`

Use this endpoint to get the summary and details of a specific conversation. You can optionally include additional conversation data such as action items, insights, outlines, transcript, or all available relationships.

...

| id | string | Yes | Conversation ID |

...

-H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"

auth.title: Authentication | Otter API Docs
highlights:
# Authentication

How your app proves who it is when calling the Otter API — and how you verify that inbound webhooks really came from Otter.

There are two directions:

| Direction | What you do | Primary mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Outbound — your app → Otter | Call REST endpoints | OAuth 2.0 access token as `Authorization: Bearer …` |
| Inbound — Otter → your app | Receive webhooks | Validate `X-HMAC-SHA256` on every request |

Exact token request/response fields live in the API reference. Code samples for webhook HMAC live in Keep webhooks secure.

## Application credentials Copy Anchor Link

Create your application through the gated self-service flow in PartnerHub, or ask your Otter contact for help when that flow is unavailable. After provisioning finishes and you can open the application, select it in Developers and open Keys for its OAuth Client ID and client secret.

Use the Client ID shown on Keys, rather than assuming it is interchangeable with an application identifier. Additional credentials have their own Client IDs. Copy a newly issued secret when it is shown; it cannot be retrieved later. Never commit secrets to source control or expose them in a browser, mobile app, or chat.

Self-service starts with a sandbox application. Check the selected application's environment and store connections before sending traffic; creating an application alone does not grant production readiness or connect a merchant store.

See Quickstart for the complete first-call path.

## Calling the Otter API (outbound) Copy Anchor Link

### Access tokens Copy Anchor Link

Request an access token from `POST /v1/auth/token` using your Client ID and client secret.

Two common OAuth 2.0 flows:

| Flow | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Client credentials | Server-to-server integration — no end-user login. Most partner integrations start here. |
| Authorization code | A merchant user must authorize your app (for example organization onboarding). Starts at `GET /v1/auth/oauth2/authorize`, then exchange the code at `/v1/auth/token`. |

Example shape (client credentials):

Request an access token

Copy Text

```
curl --request POST 'https://partners.tryotter.com/v1/auth/token' \
 --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
 --data-urlencode 'scope=ping' \
 --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
 --data-urlencode 'client_id=[CLIENT_ID]' \
 --data-urlencode 'client_secret=[CLIENT_SECRET]'
```

The response includes `access_token`, `token_type` (`bearer`), and `expires_in`. Access tokens are valid for 30 days by default. Always treat the returned `expires_in` value, in seconds, as authoritative and request a new token before that value elapses.

### Request headers Copy Anchor Link

On resource calls:

Authenticated store-scoped request

Copy Text

```
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
X-Store-Id: <store_id>
```

- `Authorization` — required on resource endpoints.
- `X-Store-Id` — required on store-scoped endpoints. Send the store identifier from your system that is linked to the authenticated application. See Stores and connections and Quickstart — connect stores.

### Scopes Copy Anchor Link

Tokens and applications are limited by scopes (for example organization or orders scopes). Request only what you need. Missing scope → authorization errors even with a valid token. Scope lists are in the API reference.

### 401 versus 503 Copy Anchor Link

- 401 — the token is missing, invalid, expired, or revoked. Request a new token before retrying.
- 503 with a `Retry-After` header — Otter could not validate the token at that moment because of a temporary internal issue. It says nothing about whether the token is valid. Retry the same request with the same token after the number of seconds in `Retry-After`, using backoff if the error repeats.

highlights:
# Generate token

Try in Playground

Client credentials in the request-body and HTTP Basic Auth are supported.

## Request Body Copy Anchor Link

`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`

1. body

Filter Properties TypeScript

The entity to request a token, following the OAuth2.0 protocol.

`client_id?` string Copy Link

The ID of the client (also known as the Application ID).

Format`uuid`

`client_secret?` string Copy Link

The secret of the client.

`grant_type*` string Copy Link

The OAuth2.0 grant types supported.

Value in`"client_credentials"``"authorization_code"`

`scope*` string Copy Link

The scope to request, multiple scopes are passed delimited by a space character.

`code?` string Copy Link

The authorization code obtained from the server when performing the authorization code flow. It is required to exchange the code for an access token that will be used to perform actions on behalf of a user.

`redirect_uri?` string Copy Link

The redirect URI that was included in the initial authorization request. The value must be an exact match of the previously used URI, otherwise the request will be rejected.

`code_verifier?` string Copy Link

If the code_challenge parameter was included in the initial authorization requests, the application must now provide the code verifier. The value is the plaintext string that was used to calculate the hash that was previously sent in the code_challenge parameter.

## Response Body Copy Anchor Link

200 400 401 422

The token was successfully generated.

`application/json`

1. response

Filter Properties TypeScript

`access_token?` string Copy Link

The auth token used when consuming the API endpoints.

`expires_in?` integer Copy Link

Token lifetime in seconds. The default is 30 days, but this returned value is authoritative for the issued token.

Format`int64`

`scope?` string Copy Link

The scopes available for the token.

`token_type?` string Copy Link

The token type is always "bearer".

Example Request

cURL curl Copy Text

```
curl -X POST 'https://partners.tryotter.com/v1/auth/token' \  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \  -d 'grant_type=client_credentials&scope=ping&client_id=e22f94b3-967c-4e26-bf39-9e364066b68b&client_secret=your-client-secret'
```

Example Response Schema 200 200 Copy Text

auth.title: Authorize with OAuth 2.0 | Otter API Docs
highlights:
# Authorize with OAuth 2.0

Try in Playground

Request a user's authorization to perform action on their behalf

## Query Parameters Copy Anchor Link

`client_id*` string Copy Link

The ID of the client (also known as the Application ID).

`redirect_uri*` string Copy Link

The URI to where the user should be redirected when the flow is successfully completed. It must be previously registered at Developer Portal in the application settings.

`response_type*` string Copy Link

Specifies the expected response type. Only "code" is accepted.

`scope*` string Copy Link

The scope to request, multiple scopes are passed delimited by a space character.

`state*` string Copy Link

Can be used to store request-specific data. The server will return the unmodified state value back to the application.

`code_challenge?` string Copy Link

A code verifier generated by the client application transformed by applying a cryptographic hash function, such as SHA-256, and encoding the result using URL-safe Base64 encoding.

`code_challenge_method?` string Copy Link

Method used to transform the code verifier. The most common method is "S256", which stands for SHA-256.

## Response Body Copy Anchor Link

302 400 401 422

The token was successfully generated.

Example Request

cURL curl Copy Text

```
curl -X GET 'https://partners.tryotter.com/v1/auth/oauth2/authorize?client_id=string&redirect_uri=string&response_type=string&scope=string&state=string'
```

Example Response 302 302

auth.title: Otter MCP Server – Help Center
highlights:
Otter Help

 October 30, 2026 21:11 Updated 

Connect AI models to Otter using Model Context Protocol (MCP). Connecting Otter MCP to your AI applications enables secure, scalable access to various language model understandings to power features like smarter summaries, contextual suggestions, and automated insights for all your Otter conversations and meetings.

Learn to connect to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Perplexity, or other platforms.

## What is Model Context Protocol (MCP)?

MCP is an open standard that allows AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT to securely access external data sources. With Otter’s MCP Server, these AI assistants can:

✅ Search your meeting transcripts across all time periods

✅ Analyze patterns and themes across multiple meetings

✅ Generate content using your actual meeting data

✅ Surface insights without leaving your AI workflow

🔑 Key advantage: Your meeting knowledge becomes instantly accessible to AI assistants, eliminating manual copy-paste and context-switching.

🔒 Security: All access is OAuth-authenticated with granular permissions. Your AI assistant can only access meetings you explicitly authorize.

...

##  Connect Otter MCP to other AI tools You may be able to connect Otter MCP to your AI tool depending on your platform 

Otter MCP can be connected to third-party AI tools that support the Model Context Protocol (MCP) using a JSON configuration file. Setup varies by platform and is managed entirely within your AI tool’s configuration. Configuration, behavior, and support depend on the specific platform you are using. Refer to your tool's documentation to connect to an MCP server.

### Before you begin

- Your AI tool must support MCP
- You should be familiar with editing JSON configuration files
- OAuth authentication is still required to connect 

### JSON Configuration file

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "otter": {
      "url": "https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### Complete setup in your AI tool

1. Add a custom MCP and configure the JSON file with the above. 
2. Connect and authenticate with your Otter account.
3. Verify the Otter MCP server appears, and tools are available. 

 Note: We’ll continue adding step-by-step guides for more AI tools. In the meantime, setup may vary by platform and is completed at your discretion.

...

## Is Otter MCP available for all AI applications? 

- We are working to release Otter MCP for all AI applications. Contact our Otter Support Team for help setting up Otter MCP with your AI application.

...

## Is there a public API key for me to set up Otter MCP for my AI application?

- We currently do not have a public API key at this time. Contact our Otter Support team for help setting up Otter MCP with your AI application.

Bring AI meeting intelligence to your customers, users, or members. Otter helps teams capture, summarize, and act on the conversations that drive their business. Help customers get more value from every conversation.

- Increase customer value

Add AI meeting notes, summaries, action items, and insights to the workflows your customers already use.
- Create revenue opportunities

Explore referral, resale, co-sell, bundled, marketplace, or other commercial models.
- Differentiate your offering

Help customers standardize on a trusted AI meeting assistant instead of fragmented individual tools.
- Support customer adoption

Work with Otter on enablement, onboarding, and best practices to help customers get value faster.

## Ways to partner

- Technology & integration partners

Build integrations that connect Otter meeting intelligence into your product, platform, or customer workflows.
- Channel, reseller & distribution partners

Bring Otter to your customers, members, or marketplace users through referral, resale, co-sell, or bundled motions.
- Referral & affiliate partners

Refer qualified customers to Otter and earn incentives for approved opportunities or new business.
- Solutions & services partners

Help customers implement, adopt, and operationalize Otter through consulting, enablement, workflow design, or managed services.

Apply

Tell us about your company, audience, customers, and partnership goals.

Connect

Our partnerships team will review your application and follow up if there may be a fit.

Launch

gate.title: Partner Hub – Otter Help Center
highlights:
#  Partner Hub 

## Overview

Partner Hub is Otter's new workspace for partners who build integrations with Otter's APIs. It's where you set up your integration, get the credentials to connect your systems to Otter, and test everything in a safe sandbox before you go live.

With Partner Hub, you're able to:

- Create an application for your integration and work in its sandbox workspace
- Get and manage the API credentials that connect your systems to Otter
- Set up webhooks so your systems are notified when events happen
- Test against stores that Otter provisions for you
- Review your requests, responses, and delivery results in logs, without needing to submit a support ticket
- See configuration changes made by your team in one place

Partner Hub Login Partner Hub is currently invitation only. You will receive an email with further instructions to set up your account

### Partner Hub Features 

Partner Hub puts the tools you need to build and test an Otter integration in one place, so you can move faster and troubleshoot on your own. The sandbox gives you a testing environment before you request production access, so you can build and test with confidence before anything touches a live restaurant.

| Partner Hub Features  | Your Benefits  |
| --- | --- |
| Application setup | Define your integration and enter its sandbox workspace. |
| API credentials and webhooks | Connect your systems to Otter and receive event notifications. |
| Test stores | Build and test against stores provisioned for you. |
| Logs and team activity | Review requests, responses, delivery results, and configuration changes without relying on a support ticket. |

## Process Overview

Once you have your login, here's the path from sign-in to testing:

- Activate your account, add your business, and create a sandbox application
- Get oriented on the home page
- Get and create your API credentials
- Set up webhooks
- Use your test stores and sign in to Otter Dashboard and Order Manager
- Review your integration logs

When you're ready to go live, certification, billing, and production access are handled with your Otter contact. Partner Hub doesn't activate production on its own at this stage.

## 1. Set up your account 

After Otter adds you as a user, follow this sequence: invitation email, set password, sign in, add business, create sandbox application.

How to activate your account, add a business, and create an application 

| Step | Process | Image |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Open the invitation email. Look for the email from no-reply@notify.tryotter.com with the subject Set up your Otter Partner Hub account, then select Set your password. |   |
| 2 | Set your password and sign in. Enter and confirm your password, then select Set password. Sign in using the email address that was invited. |   |
| 3 | Add your business. Follow the prompts to add your business to Partner Hub. |   |

## 2. Create your Sandbox Application

Your application is where you develop and test your integration. It lives in the sandbox, so nothing you do here affects live restaurants.

Steps to Create Sandbox Application:

| Step | Process | Image |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Open the application switcher and select Add application. |   |
| 2 | Choose the application type: Orders, Point of sale, or Delivery. |  |
| 3 | Enter an Application name and Description.  |   |
| 4 | Select all applicable Operating countries, then select Create. |   |

...

Some checklist items on the home page reflect later steps in the integration journey, such as going live. They don't mean you can certify or move to production on your own.

...

## 4. Get & Create API Credentials 

API Client IDs and secrets authenticate your integration's requests to Otter. They are different from the credentials you use to sign in to Otter Dashboard and Order Manager.

Steps to Get & Create API Credentials:

| Step | Process | Image |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Open Keys. Confirm you're in the right application and the Sandbox environment. Your default Client ID is visible and the secret is masked. Use the copy button to copy the Client ID. |   |
| 2 | Create additional credentials. Select Create credential and enter a unique alias (up to 100 characters). Separate credentials are useful for independent systems, such as bots or CI. Select Create credential to confirm. |    |
| 3 | Save your secret. Copy the secret from the confirmation screen and store it somewhere secure, then select Done. NOTE: The secret is shown only once. After you select Done, you won't be able to view it again. If you lose it, regenerate it. Each saved credential shows a masked secret and the time it was created, with options to regenerate or revoke it individually. |    |

...

✅ Analyze patterns and themes across multiple meetings

✅ Generate content using your actual meeting data

✅ Surface insights without leaving your AI workflow

🔑 Key advantage: Your meeting knowledge becomes instantly accessible to AI assistants, eliminating manual copy-paste and context-switching.

🔒 Security: All access is OAuth-authenticated with granular permissions. Your AI assistant can only access meetings you explicitly authorize.

##  Claude setup Learn how to set up Claude 

 Check out Otter.ai in the Claude connectors directory. 

Connect Otter MCP to Claude.

1. Go to Settings → Connectors → Browse connectors. 

 Note: If your workspace admin has already added Otter.ai, it will appear as an available connector. Click Connect and proceed directly to Step 3.
2. Go to Claude's Otter.ai page and click Connect.
3. Sign in to your Otter account. Review the info and click Authorize access to connect with Claude.
4. Otter MCP is connected to Claude.

### Enable Otter MCP tool with chat

Click on the search and tools menu in the chat box. Toggle on Otter. 

### Configure your Otter MCP tool permissions

Claude will prompt for permissions when querying using Otter MCP tools.

You can manage permissions for the Otter MCP tool in the connector settings. 

1. Under the settings Connectors, click Configure next to Otter or manage through the 3-dot menu.
2. Manage each of the tools' permissions. We recommend setting it to Always allow.

##  ChatGPT setup Learn how to set up ChatGPT 

Connect Otter MCP to ChatGPT. Otter.ai is available in the ChatGPT App Store. 

 Check out Otter.ai in the ChatGPT App Store. 

1. Sign in to the ChatGPT web version. Go to Settings. 

 Note: To connect to Otter MCP, you must currently complete the connection through the web version of Otter. Connecting directly through the desktop app is not yet supported. Once the connection is established on the web, it will automatically be available in the desktop app.
2. Go to Apps and add apps. The option may vary depending on your existing account. 
3. Go to Otter.ai in the ChatGPT App Store. 
4. Click Connect. 
5. Carefully review the information and click Connect Otter.ai. 
6. Sign in to your Otter.ai account. Carefully review the information and click Authorize access to proceed. 
7. Otter.ai is now connected to your ChatGPT account.  

Enable Otter MCP tools with ChatGPT. Now that Otter is connected, you can work from the ChatGPT web browser or the desktop app. 

- Click the + (plus icon). Click ••• More and select Otter.ai.
- Type @ and select Otter.ai. 

When starting a new chat, make sure Otter.ai is showing. If you do not see otter.ai, select it again through the steps above.

### Using Otter MCP tools with ChatGPT

Otter uses 3 tools in ChatGPT to query your meetings: 

- fetch
- get user info
- search

If prompted, accept the tool request to proceed. 

You can click any source to go directly to the Otter conversation. 

If you are experiencing any issues querying your Otter conversations, we recommend specifically mentioning the Otter tool you want to use in your query.

Manage Otter MCP settings for ChatGPT in Apps.

##  Cursor setup Learn how to set up Cursor

Make sure the connector is enabled before submitting your query. You may need to grant permissions the first time you use the provided tools. 

##  Connect Otter MCP to other AI tools You may be able to connect Otter MCP to your AI tool depending on your platform 

Otter MCP can be connected to third-party AI tools that support the Model Context Protocol (MCP) using a JSON configuration file. Setup varies by platform and is managed entirely within your AI tool’s configuration. Configuration, behavior, and support depend on the specific platform you are using. Refer to your tool's documentation to connect to an MCP server.

- You should be familiar with editing JSON configuration files

mcp.title: Otter MCP Server vs Otter API: Choose the Right Interface
highlights:
Aug 31, 2026

# Otter’s MCP Server or Otter API? Decide The Tool Calling Interface for Your Agent

Saif Ali Shaik

Founding Developer Advocate

## TL;DR

- Otter ships two official programmatic surfaces, and they are not interchangeable. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) server is read-only: search meetings, fetch a transcript, get the current user. The Public API adds channels, audio downloads, structured action items, insights, outlines, file ingestion, and webhooks.
- The availability model is inverted from most tools. The MCP server connects from a standard Otter account over OAuth; the Public API is gated to Enterprise workspaces and authenticates with Bearer API keys only, no OAuth.
- Only the API is event-driven. Otter webhooks push conversation and action-item events in real time; the MCP server is pull-only inside an active agent turn.
- Both paths hand you one credential per user. MCP gives you an OAuth token; the API gives you a static Bearer key (a maximum of two per user, 10 requests per second). Neither gives you storage, rotation, or revocation.

...

## What Otter MCP and Otter API actually are

These are two distinct objects with different design intents. The MCP server exists to drop meeting context into an interactive AI client. The API exists to move meeting data into systems on a schedule or on an event.

### Otter MCP: the hosted, read-only connector

Otter runs a provider-hosted MCP server at mcp.otter.ai/mcp. Access is OAuth-authenticated with per-meeting permissions, so an agent reads only meetings the user captured or had shared with them. The surface is deliberately small: three tools that search meetings, fetch a full transcript, and return the current user with get user info. There are no create, update, or delete tools; the server is read-only by design. Details are in Otter's MCP server documentation.

### Otter API: the Enterprise, key-based surface

The Public API is a REST surface at api.otter.ai/v1, available to Enterprise workspaces only. It authenticates with a Bearer API key created in the workspace Developer settings, capped at two keys per user and 10 requests per second. It exposes channels and members, conversations (list, retrieve, and POST to ingest a file), audio download links, workspace details, and cursor-based pagination. It also ships webhooks. The full reference is in Otter's Public API documentation.

...

### What your agent can actually do

The MCP server is strongest at retrieval-by-meaning: its search tool takes a semantic query plus filters for attendee, date range, folder, channel, and transcript keywords. The API has no semantic search endpoint; it lists and filters conversations, but it returns richer structured objects and can write.

Capability

Otter MCP

Otter API

Semantic meeting search

Yes

No (list and filter only)

Fetch full transcript

Yes

Yes (include=transcript)

AI summary

Yes (abstract_summary)

Structured action items

Limited (inside transcript text)

Yes (relationships.action_items)

Insights and outline

Limited

Yes (include=insights,outline)

No

Download audio (MP3)

Ingest a file (create conversation)

Yes (POST /conversations)

Workspace details

Yes (GET /workspace)

Write operations

No (read-only)

Yes (ingestion)

The gap is real in both directions. If your agent needs to answer "which calls mentioned pricing pushback," the MCP server does it in one call. If your agent needs the MP3, the per-meeting action items as data, or a push when a transcript is ready, only the API delivers that.

### The auth path each one puts you on

This is where Otter departs from the usual pattern. The MCP server uses OAuth 2.1 with a browser consent step, minting a token scoped to what the user authorized. The API does not support OAuth at all; it uses a static Bearer key the user generates in the dashboard. There is no public API key for the MCP server, and no OAuth for the API. The choice picks your credential type.

For a multi-tenant B2B agent, the implication is identical on both paths. Every user carries their own Otter credential: an OAuth token on the MCP path, an API key on the API path. That is N credentials to store, refresh or rotate, and revoke, regardless of which surface you chose. The token type changes; the isolation requirement does not.

# Otter.ai

> Otter.ai generic MCP server on Agent Handler. Read meeting transcripts and notes.

> Generic MCP server
> 
> Otter.ai builds and hosts this MCP server. Agent Handler proxies your agent's calls to it, so you get the same auth, tool access controls, and audit trail you get on a Merge Connector. The tool surface itself comes from Otter.ai.

Read meeting transcripts and notes.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Type | Generic MCP server, hosted by Otter.ai |
| Server URL | `https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp` |
| Authentication | OAuth |
| Tool surface | Defined by Otter.ai |
| Vendor docs | help.otter.ai |

## Authentication

Otter.ai authenticates over OAuth. Your end user approves access in Otter.ai's own consent screen during Magic Link, and Agent Handler holds the token.

## Available tools

Tools on a generic MCP server are defined by Otter.ai, not by Merge, so the list changes when Otter.ai changes it. Agent Handler discovers the current tools when the connection is made and re-discovers them on each resync, which means your agent always sees what the server actually exposes today.

To see the tools available right now, connect Otter.ai in the dashboard and open its Connector page, or read Otter.ai's own MCP documentation.
